title: Fifty-Nine Holes in Front, Two Holes Behind: Williams Survives Catalonia
title_candidates: Fifty-Nine Holes in Front, Two Holes Behind: Williams Survives Catalonia
Williams's Record Round, and the Three Days He Spent Giving It Back
The Ninth at the Stadium: One Hole, Two Trophies, One Ten
Level Par and Barely Standing: Williams Retains the Trophy in Spain
theme: A tournament won in one record-breaking afternoon and then defended, badly, for three days: Williams led for 59 holes, lost the lead for two, and got it back at the hardest hole on the trip — the same 9th at the Stadium that handed Mullin the Jacket.
tone: House voice: faithful, witty, tongue-in-cheek — Ronay/Peck register, every gag anchored to a real score. Gentle ribbing of insiders who were there.
opening_hook: Open with the bare arithmetic of the duel — Williams in front for 59 holes, Baker in front for two — and the 9th tee at PGA Catalunya Stadium where it flipped back, before Act I rewinds to the record round that made it all necessary.
foreshadow: Williams's R1 -12 (b07) is the best round in TEG history — and he banks a nine-shot cushion on day one that he will never add a single shot to again.
The 9th at the Stadium, stroke index 1 — mentioned in passing as the hardest hole of the closing course, then left loaded.
Baker arrives as the serial nearly-man: Trophy ranks of 2nd, 1st, 2nd, 2nd in the last four TEGs, and a personal-best gross +18 in R1 (b10) suggesting this might finally be the one.
Meller carries two prior Wooden Spoons into Catalonia — and posts a personal best in R2 (b13/b14) that looks, briefly, like an escape.

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, +0, by 5 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Won on day one and endured thereafter. Williams's -12 at the Tour course (b07) — the best round in TEG history to date — opened a nine-shot lead he still held after R2 and, at eight, after R3. R4 at the Stadium was a slow-motion demolition: 11 shots gone over holes 1-4 (b40), 13 more over 6-9 (b22), and at the 7th Baker went outright ahead (b04), ending Williams's 59-hole tenure at the top (b01). Two holes later the hardest hole on the course intervened: Baker took 10 at the 9th (b12), Williams took 7, and the lead came straight back (b06). Williams then bled a further 14 shots over 14-18 (b19) and still won by five (b03), finishing at level par net.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +85, by 4 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Mullin led from R1 H3, stretched it to five after Costa Brava, then collapsed at El Prat Rosa: +29, his worst gross round to date (b21), including a 9 at the 15th (b18) and a 9 at the 18th (b32) — where Baker's par took the lead by one (b02) and ended a 51-hole reign. The counterpunch came at the same 9th that settled the Trophy: Mullin's par on SI 1 against Baker's 10 put him back in front (b05). Baker drew level again at the 16th (b24) before an 8 at the last (b43) settled it: Mullin by four (b08), a fourth straight Jacket.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Bottom after R1 (+7), Meller then produced the trip's feel-good round — a personal-best -5 and personal-best gross +17 at Costa Brava (b13/b14) — which lifted him off the floor and left Neumann there instead. El Prat Rosa undid all of it inside an hour: a 10 at the 1st dropped him back to last (b27, b44) and he never climbed out, adding a 10 at the 8th (b17) and a 9 at the 17th (b28) on the way to +15. A +13 at the Stadium confirmed a third career Spoon.

headline_candidates: The Ninth at the Stadium Settles Both Trophy and Jacket
Baker Leads for Two Holes, Then Takes Ten
Spain's Premier Test, and Five Men Who Failed It
rounds.chosen_headline: The Ninth at the Stadium Settles Both Trophy and Jacket
rounds.angle: A closing round of collective disintegration on Spain's best course, resolved at the SI 1 ninth: Baker, outright leader since the 7th (b04, b01), makes 10 (b12); Williams's triple is enough to reclaim the Trophy (b06) and Mullin's par reclaims the Jacket (b05) — after which Williams bleeds 14 more shots (b19) and wins by five anyway.

players.arc: Defending champion who won this Trophy in a single afternoon — -12, the best round TEG has seen (b07) — then spent three days and one grisly Stadium round returning the money, holding on at level par by five.

Trophy ranks of 2nd, 1st, 2nd, 2nd going in; he finally took an outright lead at R4 H7 (b04), held it for two holes, made 10 at the ninth (b12), and finished runner-up in both the Trophy and the Jacket.

Reigning Wooden Spoon holder with three Jackets already in the wardrobe: survived his worst gross round to date (+29, b21) and a lost 51-hole lead (b02) to par the ninth and win a fourth straight Jacket (b08).
Produced the trip's warmest story at Costa Brava — twin personal bests (b13, b14) — and then two 10s and a 9 at El Prat Rosa dragged him to the bottom (b44) for a third career Wooden Spoon.
Jacket runner-up in three of the last four TEGs and nowhere near it here: briefly last after R2, then 12 shots gone in four holes at the Stadium (b47) including a 10 at the 3rd (b30).

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to Catalonia and four brand-new courses — nobody had a yardage, a memory or an excuse. Frame the trip as a resort bookend: R1 on PGA Catalunya's Tour course, the 'slightly more forgiving sibling', where Williams broke the TEG record; R4 on the Stadium, Spain's premier championship test, where the same resort took it all back. Costa Brava's contrasting nines (technical tree-lined front, open back) suit Meller's R2 escape; El Prat's Greg Norman Rosa, a multiple Spanish Open host, earns its billing as the carnage round.
course_history_notes: Every course was a first visit for every player — no prior TEG history exists at any of the four venues, so there are no course records, no PBs to beat and no local knowledge to blame.

The only 'course history' created here is the resort double: PGA Catalunya Tour in R1 and Stadium in R4, played by the same five men four days apart with wildly different results (Williams +20 gross then +41-equivalent carnage on the Stadium's closing five).
decisive_moments: Trophy — R4 H9 at PGA Catalunya Stadium (SI 1): Baker takes 10 (b12), Williams takes 7, and the lead returns to Williams outright (b06); he is never headed again despite bleeding 14 shots over the closing five (b19).

Green Jacket — R4 H9, the same hole: Mullin's par on the hardest hole on the course retakes the Gross lead (b05) after 51 holes lost at R3 H18 (b02), and survives Baker's level-pegging at the 16th (b24) and 8 at the last (b43).
Wooden Spoon — R3 H1 at El Prat Rosa: Meller's 10 at the opening par 5 (b27) drops him back to the bottom (b44) and he stays there for the remaining 53 holes.

payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 / How the Trophy was won
payoffs.payoff: The cushion is the entire margin: nine after R1, nine after R2, eight after R3, five at the finish — Williams adds nothing to it after day one and wins because of it (b07 → b03).

payoffs.seed: The 9th at the Stadium, stroke index 1
payoffs.payoff: Both competitions turn on the same hole in the same group: Baker's 10 (b12) hands the Trophy back to Williams (b06) and the Jacket back to Mullin (b05).

payoffs.seed: Baker the serial nearly-man, plus his R1 gross personal best
payoffs.payoff: He leads a TEG Trophy outright for the first time in this report's span at R4 H7 (b04, ending Williams's 59-hole run in b01), holds it for two holes, and ends up runner-up in both Trophy (b03) and Jacket (b08).

payoffs.seed: Meller's two prior Spoons and his R2 personal best
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 3 / How the Spoon was lost
payoffs.payoff: The Costa Brava PB (b13, b14) lifts him off the bottom for exactly one round before the 10 at El Prat's 1st (b27, b44) returns him there for good — Spoon number three (b23).

vehicle_fit_response.note: Williams's R4 disintegration is real and gets full prose weight as texture — but he won, so it isn't a tragedy; close_finish fires (margin 5, decisive R4 outright lead change at H7/H9), so the Williams–Baker duel takes the frame as dual_narrative with counterfactual riding alongside.
